title: Choose Medisc's visual world
question: The roll assigned Coverage Graphics. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Coverage Graphics
options.lineage: disc golf tournament broadcast graphics: leaderboard bugs, lower-third chyrons, hole overlays
options.thesis: Your card, produced like the Sunday final: a leaderboard grammar of bars, chips and hole-by-hole cells that refuses the white-card kit.
options.viewport: Home opens on a full-width navy chyron for the round in progress: course name as the lower-third, each player a bar with a struck score chip. Below, the hole-by-hole cell row like a TV scoreboard. Scorecard: hole overlay 'HOLE 7 · PAR 3 · 312 FT' as a bar, then each player's stroke scale 1–7 shown as ghost numerals with the chosen one struck forward.
options.risk: Reads like a sports app if the bars are timid; the world only works at full chyron commitment, with a light field ground so it survives midday sun.

raised.raise: Score entry shows every stroke value as a ghost with one struck forward; values snap, never tween.
Score chips carry contrast outlines so a birdie reads in direct sunlight.
Hole lists keep a strict numbered margin column.
Every stat tile shows its trend beside the value.

options.label: Tee Sign
options.lineage: painted-aluminium course signage at every tee
options.thesis: Every screen is a tee sign: hole number enormous, par and distance as stamped facts, the hole diagram as the map.
options.viewport: Scorecard as a sign face: the hole number fills the top third, par and distance stamped beneath, players below as engraved rows.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for a course app; signage green is close to the look you rejected, so it would need a different sign colour standard.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: enamel metro maps with disciplined 45° lines
options.thesis: A round is a line and every hole a station; the scorecard is the route diagram you trace.
options.viewport: The hole strip becomes the line: interchange circles for holes, your position a moving marker, scores as coloured ticks along the route.
options.case: Holds product clarity on hole progression; disc golfers do not identify with a subway.
options.risk: Charming for one screen, hard to carry into Stats and Settings.

options.label: Struck Cathode Gauze
options.lineage: nixie numeral stacks behind bronze anode mesh
options.thesis: All stroke values glow faintly at once; your score is the one struck forward, no boxes anywhere.
options.viewport: Scorecard as a numeral stack per player: 1 through 7 as dim ghosts, the chosen number blazing orange.
options.case: Wins clarity for score entry outright; nobody at Blair Mill identifies with a decade counter.
options.risk: Orange glow on black is the opposite of sunlight legibility; the discipline is worth more than the costume.

options.label: Variety Telop Captions
options.case: Loses both axes; scoring is not a comedy beat.
options.kept: Contrast outlines on chips for sun legibility.

options.label: Orizuru Crane Sequence
options.lineage: thirty-two numbered folds on vermilion washi
options.case: Loses both axes; a round is not a fold sequence.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.lineage: a dive profile down a volcanic wall
options.case: Loses both axes; depth has no meaning on a disc golf course.
options.kept: One vertical axis ruling every line of the scorecard grid.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.lineage: a small aircraft's six luminous instruments
options.case: Loses both axes; dials hide the numbers players want.
options.kept: Every stat shows trend as well as value.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What disc golf apps ship: white cards, rounded everything, one blue accent, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A list of cards under a search bar; the scorecard a card of rows.
